q: The Lebesgue differentiation theorem states that for f ∈ L¹_{loc}(ℝⁿ), at Lebesgue-almost every x:
opts: The Fourier series of f converges at x
exp: Lebesgue differentiation theorem: for a.e. x, the balls-average of f converges to f(x). x is a 'Lebesgue point' of f. The proof uses the Hardy-Littlewood maximal function. This makes the 'almost everywhere pointwise value' of an L¹ function well-defined.
